# Build functions

```{r}
# Feature Selection and Random Forest Optimization Functions
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# Function 1: Perform Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE)
# ------------------------------------------------------
# This function performs recursive feature elimination with cross-validation
# to identify the optimal set of predictors for a given dataset and target variable.

perform_rfe <- function(train_df, target_var = "target", recipe_obj = NULL, 
                        min_features = 5, step_size = 5, cv_folds = 10, 
                        seed_val = 1451) {
  
  # Load required packages if not already loaded
  pacman::p_load(caret, recipes)
  tidymodels_prefer()
  
  # Create a basic preprocessing recipe if none is provided
  if (is.null(recipe_obj)) {
    recipe_obj <- recipe(formula(paste(target_var, "~ .")), data = train_df)
  }
  
  # Prepare the recipe and process the training data
  prep_recipe <- prep(recipe_obj, training = train_df)
  train_processed <- bake(prep_recipe, new_data = train_df)
  
  # Configure RFE control parameters
  set.seed(seed_val)
  
  ctrl <- rfeControl(
    functions = rfFuncs,    # Random forest as base model for feature selection
    method = "cv",          # Cross-validation method
    number = cv_folds,      # Number of CV folds
    verbose = TRUE          # Display progress
  )
  
  # Define feature subsets to test
  n_features <- ncol(train_processed) - 1  # Exclude the target variable
  subsets <- seq(min_features, n_features, by = step_size)
  
  # Execute RFE with cross-validation
  set.seed(seed_val)
  rfe_results <- rfe(
    x = train_processed %>% select(-all_of(target_var)),
    y = train_processed[[target_var]],
    sizes = subsets,
    rfeControl = ctrl,
    metric = "Accuracy"     # Optimization metric (can be changed for regression tasks)
  )
  
  # Extract selected variables
  optimal_vars <- predictors(rfe_results)
  
  # Clean variable names (removing one-hot encoding suffixes)
  clean_variable_names <- function(vars) {
    unique_base_names <- character()
    
    for(var in vars) {
      # If variable contains underscore (from one-hot encoding), extract base name
      if(grepl("_", var)) {
        base_name <- strsplit(var, "_")[[1]][1]
      } else {
        base_name <- var
      }
      unique_base_names <- c(unique_base_names, base_name)
    }
    return(unique(unique_base_names))
  }
  
  cleaned_variables <- clean_variable_names(optimal_vars)
  
  # Create filtered datasets with selected variables
  train_df_filtered <- train_df %>% 
    select(all_of(target_var), all_of(cleaned_variables))
  
  # Return results as a list
  return(list(
    rfe_results = rfe_results,
    optimal_vars = optimal_vars,
    cleaned_variables = cleaned_variables,
    train_filtered = train_df_filtered
  ))
}

# Function 2: Create optimized recipe based on RFE results
# -------------------------------------------------------
# This function generates an optimized recipe using only the variables 
# selected by RFE while preserving the transformation steps from the original recipe.

create_optimized_recipe <- function(train_df_filtered, target_var = "target",
                                   unknown_vars = c("EntryAgeBeforeOne", 
                                                    "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily", 
                                                    "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren"),
                                   impute_vars = c("AffordCostBaseline", 
                                                   "Taux.de.couv.global",
                                                   "NumberChildren", 
                                                   "PrescriptiveNorm"),
                                   yeojohnson_vars = c("AffordCostBaseline", 
                                                      "MotherHealthIndex",
                                                      "BabyHealthIndex", 
                                                      "NumberChildren", 
                                                      "OpportunityCosts", 
                                                      "MonthlyDaycareFees",
                                                      "PrescriptiveNorm"),
                                   knn_neighbors = 5) {
  
  # Get the selected variables from the filtered dataframe
  selected_vars <- setdiff(names(train_df_filtered), target_var)
  
  # Compute intersections with transformation variables
  unknown_vars_filtered <- intersect(unknown_vars, selected_vars)
  impute_vars_filtered <- intersect(impute_vars, selected_vars)
  yeojohnson_vars_filtered <- intersect(yeojohnson_vars, selected_vars)
  
  # Initialize the recipe with the filtered data
  optimized_recipe <- recipe(formula(paste(target_var, "~ .")), 
                             data = train_df_filtered)
  
  # Add transformation steps conditionally based on selected variables
  # Step 1: Handle unknown values for categorical variables
  if (length(unknown_vars_filtered) > 0) {
    optimized_recipe <- optimized_recipe %>% 
      step_unknown(all_of(unknown_vars_filtered))
  }
  
  # Step 2: Create dummy variables for all nominal predictors
  optimized_recipe <- optimized_recipe %>%
    step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)
  
  # Step 3: Normalize numeric predictors
  optimized_recipe <- optimized_recipe %>%
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
  
  # Step 4: KNN imputation for variables with missing values
  if (length(impute_vars_filtered) > 0) {
    optimized_recipe <- optimized_recipe %>% 
      step_impute_knn(all_of(impute_vars_filtered), neighbors = knn_neighbors)
  }
  
  # Step 5: Apply Yeo-Johnson transformation for skewed variables
  if (length(yeojohnson_vars_filtered) > 0) {
    optimized_recipe <- optimized_recipe %>% 
      step_YeoJohnson(all_of(yeojohnson_vars_filtered))
  }
  
  return(optimized_recipe)
}

# Function 3: Tune random forest model with selected features
# ----------------------------------------------------------
# This function tunes a random forest model using the optimized recipe
# and returns the best model based on cross-validation results.

tune_random_forest <- function(train_df_filtered, test_df = NULL, target_var = "target",
                              recipe_obj, cv_folds = 10, cv_repeats = 5,
                              grid_size = 150, var_range =  0.75, n_cores = NULL, seed_val = 30,
                              engine = "partykit") {
  
  # Load required packages
  pacman::p_load(doParallel)
  tidymodels_prefer()
  
  # Filter test data if provided
  if (!is.null(test_df)) {
    selected_vars <- setdiff(names(train_df_filtered), target_var)
    test_df_filtered <- test_df %>% 
      select(all_of(target_var), all_of(selected_vars))
  } else {
    test_df_filtered <- NULL
  }
  
  # Define the random forest model specification with tunable parameters
  rf_spec <- rand_forest(
    mtry = tune(),       # Number of variables randomly sampled at each split
    trees = tune(),      # Number of trees in the forest
    min_n = tune()       # Minimum node size
  ) %>%
    set_mode("classification") %>%
    set_engine(engine)
  
  # Create a workflow with the recipe and model
  rf_workflow <- workflow() %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_obj) %>%
    add_model(rf_spec)
  
  # Extract and finalize parameter set for tuning
  rf_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_spec) %>%
    finalize(train_df_filtered)
  
  # Create Latin Hypercube sampling grid for efficient parameter space exploration
  set.seed(seed_val)
  rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
    rf_params,
    size = grid_size,
    variogram_range = var_range,
    original = TRUE
  )
  
  # Define cross-validation strategy
  set.seed(seed_val)
  cv_folds_obj <- vfold_cv(
    train_df_filtered, 
    v = cv_folds, 
    repeats = cv_repeats, 
    strata = sym(target_var)  # Stratified sampling preserves class distribution
  )
  
  # Define performance metrics
  rf_metrics <- metric_set(accuracy)
  
  # Set up parallel processing if specified
  if (!is.null(n_cores)) {
    if (n_cores > 1) {
      cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
      registerDoParallel(cl)
      on.exit(stopCluster(cl))
    }
  } else {
    registerDoParallel()
  }
  
  # Tune the model with grid search
  rf_tune_results <- rf_workflow %>%
    tune_grid(
      resamples = cv_folds_obj,
      grid = rf_grid,
      metrics = rf_metrics
    )
  
  # Select the best hyperparameter configuration
  rf_best_params <- select_best(rf_tune_results)
  
  # Finalize the model with best parameters
  rf_final_spec <- finalize_model(rf_spec, rf_best_params)
  
  # Update workflow with the finalized model
  rf_final_workflow <- rf_workflow %>%
    update_model(rf_final_spec)
  
  # Fit the final model on the training set
  rf_final_fit <- rf_final_workflow %>%
    fit(data = train_df_filtered)
  
  # Evaluate on test set if provided
  if (!is.null(test_df_filtered)) {
    test_performance <- rf_final_fit %>%
      predict(test_df_filtered) %>%
      bind_cols(test_df_filtered) %>%
      metrics(truth = !!sym(target_var), estimate = .pred_class)
  } else {
    test_performance <- NULL
  }
  
  # Return results
  return(list(
    tuning_results = rf_tune_results,
    best_params = rf_best_params,
    final_workflow = rf_final_workflow,
    final_fit = rf_final_fit,
    test_performance = test_performance
  ))
}

# Function 4: Generate SHAP values and feature importance
# ------------------------------------------------------
# This function calculates SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values
# to interpret the random forest model and visualize feature importance.

calculate_shapley_importance <- function(model_fit, test_df, target_var = "target", 
                                        n_samples = 50, seed_val = 1995) {
  
  # Load required packages
  pacman::p_load(DALEXtra, forcats, ggplot2)
  
  # Create explainer object for the model
  explainer <- explain_tidymodels(
    model = model_fit,
    data = test_df %>% select(-all_of(target_var)),
    y = test_df[[target_var]]
  )
  
  # Calculate SHAP values
  set.seed(seed_val)
  shap_values <- predict_parts(
    explainer = explainer,
    new_observation = test_df %>% select(-all_of(target_var)),
    type = "shap",
    B = n_samples  # Number of samples for approximation
  )
  
  # Calculate average SHAP values per variable
  average_shapley <- shap_values %>% 
    group_by(variable) %>% 
    summarise(contribution = mean(contribution)) %>% 
    arrange(desc(abs(contribution)))
  
  # Prepare data for visualization
  shap_plot_data <- shap_values %>%
    group_by(variable) %>%
    mutate(mean_val = mean(contribution)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, abs(mean_val)))
  
  # Create feature importance plot
  shap_plot <- shap_plot_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(contribution, variable, fill = mean_val > 0)) +
    geom_col(data = ~distinct(., variable, mean_val), 
             aes(mean_val, variable), 
             alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(
      y = NULL, 
      x = "SHAP Value (impact on model output)",
      title = "Feature Importance Based on SHAP Values",
      subtitle = "Features are ordered by mean absolute SHAP value"
    )
  
  # Return results
  return(list(
    explainer = explainer,
    shap_values = shap_values,
    average_shapley = average_shapley,
    plot_data = shap_plot_data,
    importance_plot = shap_plot
  ))
}

# For numerical predictors 


perform_rfe_reg <- function(train_df, target_var = "target", recipe_obj = NULL, 
                             min_features = 5, step_size = 5, cv_folds = 10, 
                             seed_val = 1451) {
  
  pacman::p_load(caret, recipes)
  tidymodels_prefer()
  
  if (is.null(recipe_obj)) {
    recipe_obj <- recipe(formula(paste(target_var, "~ .")), data = train_df)
  }
  
  prep_recipe <- prep(recipe_obj, training = train_df)
  train_processed <- bake(prep_recipe, new_data = train_df)
  
  set.seed(seed_val)
  
  # rfFuncs in caret auto-detects regression vs classification based on
  # the class of y, but we need to switch the control's summary function
  # and the optimization metric to RMSE
  ctrl <- rfeControl(
    functions = rfFuncs,
    method = "cv",
    number = cv_folds,
    verbose = TRUE
  )
  
  n_features <- ncol(train_processed) - 1
  subsets <- seq(min_features, n_features, by = step_size)
  
  set.seed(seed_val)
  rfe_results <- rfe(
    x = train_processed %>% select(-all_of(target_var)),
    y = train_processed[[target_var]],   # must be numeric for regression RFE
    sizes = subsets,
    rfeControl = ctrl,
    metric = "RMSE",       # switched from Accuracy
    maximize = FALSE       # lower RMSE is better
  )
  
  optimal_vars <- predictors(rfe_results)
  
  clean_variable_names <- function(vars) {
    unique_base_names <- character()
    for (var in vars) {
      if (grepl("_", var)) {
        base_name <- strsplit(var, "_")[[1]][1]
      } else {
        base_name <- var
      }
      unique_base_names <- c(unique_base_names, base_name)
    }
    return(unique(unique_base_names))
  }
  
  cleaned_variables <- clean_variable_names(optimal_vars)
  
  train_df_filtered <- train_df %>% 
    select(all_of(target_var), all_of(cleaned_variables))
  
  return(list(
    rfe_results = rfe_results,
    optimal_vars = optimal_vars,
    cleaned_variables = cleaned_variables,
    train_filtered = train_df_filtered
  ))
}

tune_random_forest_reg <- function(train_df_filtered, test_df = NULL, target_var = "target",
                                    recipe_obj, cv_folds = 10, cv_repeats = 5,
                                    grid_size = 150, var_range = 0.75, n_cores = NULL, seed_val = 30,
                                    engine = "partykit") {
  
  pacman::p_load(doParallel)
  tidymodels_prefer()
  
  if (!is.null(test_df)) {
    selected_vars <- setdiff(names(train_df_filtered), target_var)
    test_df_filtered <- test_df %>% 
      select(all_of(target_var), all_of(selected_vars))
  } else {
    test_df_filtered <- NULL
  }
  
  rf_spec <- rand_forest(
    mtry = tune(),
    trees = tune(),
    min_n = tune()
  ) %>%
    set_mode("regression") %>%       # switched from classification
    set_engine(engine)
  
  rf_workflow <- workflow() %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_obj) %>%
    add_model(rf_spec)
  
  rf_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_spec) %>%
    finalize(train_df_filtered)
  
  set.seed(seed_val)
  rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
    rf_params,
    size = grid_size,
    variogram_range = var_range,
    original = TRUE
  )
  
  set.seed(seed_val)
  # strata on a continuous target works fine in vfold_cv: it bins internally
  cv_folds_obj <- vfold_cv(
    train_df_filtered, 
    v = cv_folds, 
    repeats = cv_repeats, 
    strata = sym(target_var)
  )
  
  rf_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae)   # switched from accuracy
  
  if (!is.null(n_cores)) {
    if (n_cores > 1) {
      cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
      registerDoParallel(cl)
      on.exit(stopCluster(cl))
    }
  } else {
    registerDoParallel()
  }
  
  rf_tune_results <- rf_workflow %>%
    tune_grid(
      resamples = cv_folds_obj,
      grid = rf_grid,
      metrics = rf_metrics
    )
  
  # select_best needs a metric for regression; default to rmse, minimized
  rf_best_params <- select_best(rf_tune_results, metric = "rmse")
  
  rf_final_spec <- finalize_model(rf_spec, rf_best_params)
  
  rf_final_workflow <- rf_workflow %>%
    update_model(rf_final_spec)
  
  rf_final_fit <- rf_final_workflow %>%
    fit(data = train_df_filtered)
  
  if (!is.null(test_df_filtered)) {
    test_performance <- rf_final_fit %>%
      predict(test_df_filtered) %>%        # yields .pred, not .pred_class
      bind_cols(test_df_filtered) %>%
      metrics(truth = !!sym(target_var), estimate = .pred)
  } else {
    test_performance <- NULL
  }
  
  return(list(
    tuning_results = rf_tune_results,
    best_params = rf_best_params,
    final_workflow = rf_final_workflow,
    final_fit = rf_final_fit,
    test_performance = test_performance
  ))
}

```

# Intention

For the sake of the demonstration, we use the code without the functions previously defined.

```{r}
# Charger les packages nécessaires
p_load(caret)

data <- MLDummified %>% filter(!is.na(Intention)) %>% 
  mutate(target = factor(Intention, labels = c("No", "Yes"))) %>%   # the idea db we would be working with in the end
 select(-c(Assignment, MovedOut, ECSApp, ECSUseYes, Intention, EntryAgeBeforeOne, BabyHealthIndex, MotherHealthIndex, SocialCriteriaYes,RegistrationOnlineOnly ))
# Create a subset with the sociodemo and the predictors
# Cleaning the data

tidymodels_prefer()

# Take a look at the data with skimr
s <- skim(data)
print(s, include_summary = FALSE)
# We have NA for ECSIdealAgeEntryBaseline, TrustCreche, BreastFeedLength, NormsOpposedN,  NumberChildren we may want to impute them


# Keep 20% of the observations for the test set.
set.seed(1451)
credit_split <- initial_split(data, prop = 0.8)
train_df <- training(credit_split)
test_df <- testing(credit_split)


# 1. Appliquer d'abord votre recette pour imputer les valeurs manquantes
# Créer et préparer la recette
preprocess_recipe  <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train_df)  %>%
  step_unknown(AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily, 
               AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%

  step_impute_knn(
                  Taux.de.couv.global,
                  NumberChildren,

  step_YeoJohnson(
                  NumberChildren, 
                  OpportunityCosts,

                  PrescriptiveNorm
                  #BreastFeedLength,
                  #NumberChildren
                  ) # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values


# Préparer les données (training et test)

train_processed <- bake(prep_recipe, new_data = train_df)


# 2. Maintenant utiliser ces données prétraitées pour RFE
# Configuration du contrôle pour RFE-CV
ctrl <- rfeControl(
  functions = rfFuncs,
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Définir les sous-ensembles de caractéristiques à tester
n_features <- ncol(train_processed) - 1  # Exclure la cible
subsets <- seq(5, n_features, by = 5)

# Exécuter RFE-CV avec les données prétraitées
set.seed(1451)
rfe_results <- rfe(
  x = train_processed %>% select(-target),
  y = train_processed$target,
  sizes = subsets,
  rfeControl = ctrl,
  metric = "Accuracy"
)

# Afficher les résultats
print(rfe_results)

# Visualiser les résultats
plot(rfe_results, type = c("g", "o"))  # Graphique des performances par taille de sous-ensemble

# Obtenir les variables sélectionnées
optimal_vars <- predictors(rfe_results)
print(optimal_vars)

# Visualiser l'importance des variables sélectionnées
varimp_data <- varImp(rfe_results)
plot(varimp_data)

# Remove the suffixes due to step dummy 

# clean the variables names to get a vector of variables
# Create a function to do that
clean_variable_names <- function(vars) {
  # vector to store the names
  unique_base_names <- character()
  
  for(var in vars) {
    # Use the underscore as an indication of the variables to clean
    if(grepl("_", var)) {
      base_name <- strsplit(var, "_")[[1]][1]
    } else {
      base_name <- var
    }
    unique_base_names <- c(unique_base_names, base_name)
  }
  return(unique(unique_base_names))
  
}

cleaned_variables_intention <- clean_variable_names(optimal_vars)

# Filter train_df to keep only the selected variables

  select(target, all_of(cleaned_variables_intention))
# Filter train_df to keep only the selected variables
test_df_filtered <- test_df %>% 
  select(target, all_of(cleaned_variables_intention))

# Then we want to do the relevant transformation, but step_.. is a bit tricky, we do this by hand

# 1. D'abord, calculer toutes vos intersections en amont
unknown_vars <- intersect(c("EntryAgeBeforeOne", "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily", 
                         "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren"), cleaned_variables_intention)

impute_vars <- intersect(c("AffordCostBaseline", "Taux.de.couv.global",
                         "NumberChildren", "PrescriptiveNorm"), cleaned_variables_intention)

yeojohnson_vars <- intersect(c("AffordCostBaseline", "MotherHealthIndex",
                             "BabyHealthIndex", "NumberChildren", 
                             "OpportunityCosts", "MonthlyDaycareFees",
                             "PrescriptiveNorm"), cleaned_variables_intention)

# 2. Utiliser train_df_filtered (celui qui contient déjà uniquement les variables sélectionnées)
rf_recipe_rfe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train_df_filtered)

# 3. Ajouter les étapes conditionnellement
if (length(unknown_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_unknown(all_of(unknown_vars))
}

# Continuer avec les autres étapes
rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

if (length(impute_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_impute_knn(all_of(impute_vars), neighbors = 5)
}

if (length(yeojohnson_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_YeoJohnson(all_of(yeojohnson_vars))
}

# Continuer avec votre code de réglage de modèle, mais en utilisant la recette optimisée par RFE-CV
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), # 100 is a low side. Do at least 150 
                       trees = tune(), # if I tune it, it takes forever to run
                       min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>% # IMPORTANT! It can also deal with classes and influence the loss function
  set_engine("partykit")

# Flux de travail avec les caractéristiques sélectionnées
initial_flow_rfe <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(rf_recipe_rfe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)


# In the REAL DEFINITIVE VERSION you should also tune the number of trees, or at least generate 150 of them.

# tuned with 50 latin hypercube: mtry 4 1636 trees min_n 39




# The argument finalize is key because tidymodels needs to look
# at the data to figure out how many features there are.

# We need to tell tidymodels which parameters need to be tuned. It can conveniently be done with this chunk of code

# In this version we are not tuning the number of trees, but we could.
# We tune mtry and min_n the number of obs in each terminal leaves (you don't want one leaf == 1 obs that's overfitting)
# mtry is the number of features that are randomly selected at each split. It is a good idea to tune it because it can have a big impact on the performance of the model
# Doing this is an argument if I have a lot of predictors/features. At each round, it is only a subsample of predictors that is used. 
rf_para <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_spec) %>% # extract the tuning parameters
  finalize(train_df) # here we have only 2 because we set trees to 100 not tune()
# finalize(train): we need to know the maximum number of features we could fit because it has not looked at the data yet
# it tells tidymodel that he can look at the data quickly to see how many features there are in the data

set.seed(20) # for reproducibility

# Set the tuning grid
# The tuning grid is the set of values of the tuning parameters we seek to evaluate. The larger the better
rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(rf_para,  # we use a latin hypercube here. 
                                size = 150, # 25 random combinations of mtry and min_n LOW! Increase in real life. There are good chances that the "true" combination is not in there
                                variogram_range = 0.75, # explore the space of the hyperparameters
                                original = TRUE)
set.seed(30)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_df, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = target) # stratified CV

rf_metrics <- metric_set(accuracy) # classification task

doParallel::registerDoParallel() # used parallel cores to run the computation

# tune the model, with the cross validation method defined, the grid and the metrics you set
rf_tune <- initial_flow_rfe %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds, grid = rf_grid, metrics = rf_metrics)


# select the best parameters for the model the tuning found
rf_best <- select_best(rf_tune)
rf_best# Trees again with X features at each time and X obs at terminal leaves
# 34 features, and 19 obs in terminal leaves

# Update the model with the best parameters found
rf_updated <- finalize_model(rf_spec,
                             rf_best) 

# add this to the initial workflow
workflow_new <- initial_flow_rfe %>%
  update_model(rf_updated)

# DALEX want to know a couple of things in the explainer
explainer <- explain_tidymodels( # create the  explainer
  model = rf_fit_final, # what is the model

)


# SHAPLY VALUES
library(forcats)

set.seed(1995)
shap <- predict_parts(explainer = explainer,
                      new_observation = test_df_filtered[, !(names(test_df_filtered) %in% "target")], # remove the target
                      type = "shap", 
                      B = 50)

average_shapley <- shap %>% 
  group_by(variable) %>% 
  summarise(contribution = mean(contribution)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(abs(contribution)))


shap %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(mean_val = mean(contribution)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, abs(mean_val))) %>% # reorder the variables according to their contribution in term of their absolute value
  ggplot(aes(contribution, variable, fill = mean_val > 0)) +
  geom_col(data = ~distinct(., variable, mean_val), 
           aes(mean_val, variable), 
           alpha = 0.5, fill = "skyblue") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, fill = "skyblue") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()


shap <- shap %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(mean_val = mean(contribution)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, abs(mean_val)))

 # Level of comprehension creates pb
# Run Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition

                     data = oaxaca_data,
                     R = 100)  # Number of bootstrap repetitions

# résultats décomp agrégée
round(oax_decomp$twofold$overall[, c(1,2,4)], 3)# 3 and 5 are SD

# Diff -0.14 : coeff A (low) : 0.73; B : 0.88
# 0: low SES 
# -0.17



plot(oax_decomp, decomposition = "twofold", group.weight = 1) # reference is high SES 
plot(oax_decomp, decomposition = "twofold", group.weight = -2) # weighted 

plot(oax_decomp, components = c("endowments","coefficients"))


```

We need to rely on the weighted averages because there is not the same number of low- and high-SES.

Using the classical OB estimator, we explain `r round(oax_decomp$twofold$overall[6,2]*100 / oax_decomp$y$y.diff , 4)`% of the observed differences, and there is a `r 100-round(oax_decomp$twofold$overall[6,2]*100 / oax_decomp$y$y.diff , 2)`% of the difference in unexplained (`r round(oax_decomp$twofold$overall[3,3], 3)` percentage point unexplained part.

```{r}

# Load all necessary packages with p_load
pacman::p_load(tidymodels, caret, recipes, DALEXtra, ggplot2, forcats, doParallel)

# Load your dataset (replace with your actual data loading code)
# data <- read_csv("your_data.csv")

# 1. Prepare your data
# Assuming data is already loaded and contains your variables


# Cleaning the data
work_df <- MLDummified %>% 
  filter(!is.na(ECSApp)) %>% mutate(Application = ifelse(ECSApp == 1,"Yes", "No")) %>% 
  mutate(target = factor(Application, labels = c("No", "Yes"))
  ) %>% 
 select(-c( ECSApp, ECSUseYes, Application))

# Take a look at the data with skimr
s <- skim(work_df)
print(s, include_summary = FALSE)

# Keep 20% of the observations for the test set.
set.seed(9998)
data_split <- initial_split(work_df, prop = 0.8, strata = target)
train_df <- training(data_split)
test_df <- testing(data_split)

# 2. Define your base recipe with all relevant data transformations
base_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train_df) %>%
  step_unknown(EntryAgeBeforeOne,
               AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily, 
               AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
  step_impute_knn(
                  Taux.de.couv.global,
                  NumberChildren,
                  PrescriptiveNorm,
                  neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(
                  MotherHealthIndex,
                  BabyHealthIndex,
                  NumberChildren, 
                  OpportunityCosts,

                  PrescriptiveNorm)

# 3. Perform Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE)
rfe_results <- perform_rfe(
  train_df = train_df,
  target_var = "target",
  recipe_obj = base_recipe,
  min_features = 5,
  step_size = 5,
  cv_folds = 10,
  seed_val = 1451
)

# Print RFE results
print(rfe_results$rfe_results)
cat("Selected features:", paste(rfe_results$cleaned_variables, collapse = ", "), "\n")
plot(rfe_results$rfe_results, type = c("g", "o") )

# 4. Create an optimized recipe using only the selected features
# Define variables that require special transformations
unknown_vars <- c("EntryAgeBeforeOne", "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily", "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren")
impute_vars <- c("AffordCostBaseline", "Taux.de.couv.global", "NumberChildren", "PrescriptiveNorm")
yeojohnson_vars <- c("AffordCostBaseline", "MotherHealthIndex", "BabyHealthIndex", 
                     "NumberChildren", "OpportunityCosts", "MonthlyDaycareFees", "PrescriptiveNorm")

# Create the optimized recipe
optimized_recipe <- create_optimized_recipe(
  train_df_filtered = rfe_results$train_filtered,
  target_var = "target",
  unknown_vars = unknown_vars,
  impute_vars = impute_vars,
  yeojohnson_vars = yeojohnson_vars,
  knn_neighbors = 5
)

# 5. Tune a random forest model with the optimized recipe
rf_tuned <- tune_random_forest(
  train_df_filtered = rfe_results$train_filtered,
  test_df = test_df,
  target_var = "target",
  recipe_obj = optimized_recipe,
  cv_folds = 10,
  cv_repeats = 5,
  var_range = 0.75,
  grid_size = 150,  # Number of hyperparameter combinations to test
  n_cores = NULL,   # Use all available cores
  seed_val = 30,
  engine = "partykit"
)

# Print tuning results
print(rf_tuned$best_params)
print(rf_tuned$test_performance)

# 6. Calculate and visualize SHAP values for model interpretation
shap_results <- calculate_shapley_importance(
  model_fit = rf_tuned$final_fit,
  test_df = test_df %>% select(target, all_of(rfe_results$cleaned_variables)),
  target_var = "target",
  n_samples = 50,
  seed_val = 1995
)

# Display the average SHAP values (feature importance)
print(shap_results$average_shapley)

# Plot feature importance
print(shap_results$importance_plot)
```

# Remove the suffixes due to step dummy 

# clean the variables names to get a vector of variables
# Create a function to do that
clean_variable_names <- function(vars) {
  # vector to store the names
  unique_base_names <- character()
  
  for(var in vars) {
    # Use the underscore as an indication of the variables to clean
    if(grepl("_", var)) {
      base_name <- strsplit(var, "_")[[1]][1]
    } else {
      base_name <- var
    }
    unique_base_names <- c(unique_base_names, base_name)
  }
  return(unique(unique_base_names))
  
}

cleaned_variables_intention <- clean_variable_names(optimal_vars)

# Filter train_df to keep only the selected variables

  select(target, all_of(cleaned_variables_intention))

# Then we want to do the relevant transformation, but step_.. is a bit tricky, we do this by hand

                         "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren"), cleaned_variables_intention)

yeojohnson_vars <- intersect(c("AffordCostBaseline", "MotherHealthIndex",
                             "BabyHealthIndex", "NumberChildren", 
                             "OpportunityCosts", "MonthlyDaycareFees",
                             "PrescriptiveNorm"), cleaned_variables_intention)

# 2. Utiliser train_df_filtered (celui qui contient déjà uniquement les variables sélectionnées)
rf_recipe_rfe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train_df_filtered)

# 3. Ajouter les étapes conditionnellement
if (length(unknown_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_unknown(all_of(unknown_vars))
}

# Continuer avec les autres étapes
rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

if (length(impute_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_impute_knn(all_of(impute_vars), neighbors = 5)
}

if (length(yeojohnson_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_YeoJohnson(all_of(yeojohnson_vars))
}

# Continuer avec votre code de réglage de modèle, mais en utilisant la recette optimisée par RFE-CV

# Flux de travail avec les caractéristiques sélectionnées
initial_flow_rfe <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(rf_recipe_rfe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)


# In the REAL DEFINITIVE VERSION you should also tune the number of trees, or at least generate 150 of them.
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), # 100 is a low side. Do at least 150 
                       trees = tune(), # if I tune it, it takes forever to run
                       min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>% # IMPORTANT! It can also deal with classes and influence the loss function
  set_engine("partykit")

# tuned with 50 latin hypercube: mtry 4 1636 trees min_n 39




# The argument finalize is key because tidymodels needs to look
# at the data to figure out how many features there are.

# We need to tell tidymodels which parameters need to be tuned. It can conveniently be done with this chunk of code

# In this version we are not tuning the number of trees, but we could.
# We tune mtry and min_n the number of obs in each terminal leaves (you don't want one leaf == 1 obs that's overfitting)
# mtry is the number of features that are randomly selected at each split. It is a good idea to tune it because it can have a big impact on the performance of the model
# Doing this is an argument if I have a lot of predictors/features. At each round, it is only a subsample of predictors that is used. 
rf_para <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_spec) %>% # extract the tuning parameters
  finalize(train_df) # here we have only 2 because we set trees to 100 not tune()
# finalize(train): we need to know the maximum number of features we could fit because it has not looked at the data yet
# it tells tidymodel that he can look at the data quickly to see how many features there are in the data

set.seed(20) # for reproducibility

# Set the tuning grid
# The tuning grid is the set of values of the tuning parameters we seek to evaluate. The larger the better
rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(rf_para,  # we use a latin hypercube here. 
                                size = 150, # 25 random combinations of mtry and min_n LOW! Increase in real life. There are good chances that the "true" combination is not in there
                                variogram_range = 0.75, # explore the space of the hyperparameters
                                original = TRUE)
set.seed(30)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_df, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = target) # stratified CV

rf_metrics <- metric_set(accuracy) # classification task

doParallel::registerDoParallel() # used parallel cores to run the computation

# tune the model, with the cross validation method defined, the grid and the metrics you set
rf_tune <- initial_flow_rfe %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds, grid = rf_grid, metrics = rf_metrics)


# select the best parameters for the model the tuning found
rf_best <- select_best(rf_tune)
rf_best# Trees again with X features at each time and X obs at terminal leaves
# 34 features, and 19 obs in terminal leaves

# Update the model with the best parameters found
rf_updated <- finalize_model(rf_spec,
                             rf_best) 

# add this to the initial workflow
workflow_new <- initial_flow_rfe %>%
  update_model(rf_updated)

# Fit the model on the training set
rf_fit_final <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = train_df_filtered) # fit on the training set

# Fit the model on the test set to evaluate performance
# Performance on the test set
rf_fit_final %>%
  predict(test_df_filtered) %>%
  bind_cols(test_df_filtered) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred_class)
# the accuracy is great but the kappa not that much (average)
# see if tuning the trees improve this in the future

# Charger les packages nécessaires
p_load(caret)

data <- MLDummified %>% filter(!is.na(EntryAgeBeforeOne)) %>% 
  mutate(target = factor(EntryAgeBeforeOne, labels = c("After One", "Before One"))) %>%   # the idea db we would be working with in the end
 select(-c(Assignment,  ECSApp, ECSUseYes, Intention, EntryAgeBeforeOne, BabyHealthIndex, MotherHealthIndex ))
# Create a subset with the sociodemo and the predictors
# Cleaning the data

tidymodels_prefer()

# Take a look at the data with skimr
s <- skim(data)
print(s, include_summary = FALSE)
# We have NA for ECSIdealAgeEntryBaseline, TrustCreche, BreastFeedLength, NormsOpposedN,  NumberChildren we may want to impute them


# Keep 20% of the observations for the test set.
set.seed(1451)
credit_split <- initial_split(data, prop = 0.8)
train_df <- training(credit_split)
test_df <- testing(credit_split)


# 1. Appliquer d'abord votre recette pour imputer les valeurs manquantes
# Créer et préparer la recette
preprocess_recipe  <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train_df)  %>%
  step_unknown(AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily, 
               AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
  step_impute_knn(
                  Taux.de.couv.global,
                  NumberChildren,
                  PrescriptiveNorm,
                  neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(
                  NumberChildren, 
                  OpportunityCosts,

                  PrescriptiveNorm
                  #BreastFeedLength,
                  #NumberChildren
                  ) # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values


# Préparer les données (training et test)
prep_recipe <- prep(preprocess_recipe, training = train_df)
train_processed <- bake(prep_recipe, new_data = train_df)


# 2. Maintenant utiliser ces données prétraitées pour RFE
# Configuration du contrôle pour RFE-CV
ctrl <- rfeControl(
  functions = rfFuncs,
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Définir les sous-ensembles de caractéristiques à tester
n_features <- ncol(train_processed) - 1  # Exclure la cible
subsets <- seq(5, n_features, by = 5)

# Exécuter RFE-CV avec les données prétraitées
set.seed(1451)
rfe_results <- rfe(
  x = train_processed %>% select(-target),
  y = train_processed$target,
  sizes = subsets,
  rfeControl = ctrl,
  metric = "Accuracy"
)

# Afficher les résultats
print(rfe_results)

# Visualiser les résultats
plot(rfe_results, type = c("g", "o"))  # Graphique des performances par taille de sous-ensemble

# Obtenir les variables sélectionnées
optimal_vars <- predictors(rfe_results)
print(optimal_vars)

# Visualiser l'importance des variables sélectionnées
varimp_data <- varImp(rfe_results)
plot(varimp_data)

# Remove the suffixes due to step dummy 

# clean the variables names to get a vector of variables
# Create a function to do that
clean_variable_names <- function(vars) {
  # vector to store the names
  unique_base_names <- character()
  
  for(var in vars) {
    # Use the underscore as an indication of the variables to clean
    if(grepl("_", var)) {
      base_name <- strsplit(var, "_")[[1]][1]
    } else {
      base_name <- var
    }
    unique_base_names <- c(unique_base_names, base_name)
  }
  return(unique(unique_base_names))
  
}

cleaned_variables_intention <- clean_variable_names(optimal_vars)

# Filter train_df to keep only the selected variables
train_df_filtered <- train_df %>% 
  select(target, all_of(cleaned_variables_intention))
# Filter train_df to keep only the selected variables
test_df_filtered <- test_df %>% 
  select(target, all_of(cleaned_variables_intention))

# Then we want to do the relevant transformation, but step_.. is a bit tricky, we do this by hand

# 1. D'abord, calculer toutes vos intersections en amont
unknown_vars <- intersect(c("EntryAgeBeforeOne", "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily", 
                         "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren"), cleaned_variables_intention)

impute_vars <- intersect(c("AffordCostBaseline", "Taux.de.couv.global",
                         "NumberChildren", "PrescriptiveNorm"), cleaned_variables_intention)

yeojohnson_vars <- intersect(c("AffordCostBaseline", "MotherHealthIndex",
                             "BabyHealthIndex", "NumberChildren", 
                             "OpportunityCosts", "MonthlyDaycareFees",
                             "PrescriptiveNorm"), cleaned_variables_intention)

# 2. Utiliser train_df_filtered (celui qui contient déjà uniquement les variables sélectionnées)
rf_recipe_rfe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train_df_filtered)

# 3. Ajouter les étapes conditionnellement
if (length(unknown_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_unknown(all_of(unknown_vars))
}

# Continuer avec les autres étapes
rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

if (length(impute_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_impute_knn(all_of(impute_vars), neighbors = 5)
}

if (length(yeojohnson_vars) > 0) {
  rf_recipe_rfe <- rf_recipe_rfe %>% 
    step_YeoJohnson(all_of(yeojohnson_vars))
}

# Continuer avec votre code de réglage de modèle, mais en utilisant la recette optimisée par RFE-CV
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), # 100 is a low side. Do at least 150 
                       trees = tune(), # if I tune it, it takes forever to run
                       min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>% # IMPORTANT! It can also deal with classes and influence the loss function
  set_engine("partykit")

# Flux de travail avec les caractéristiques sélectionnées
initial_flow_rfe <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(rf_recipe_rfe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)


# In the REAL DEFINITIVE VERSION you should also tune the number of trees, or at least generate 150 of them.

# tuned with 50 latin hypercube: mtry 4 1636 trees min_n 39




# The argument finalize is key because tidymodels needs to look
# at the data to figure out how many features there are.

# We need to tell tidymodels which parameters need to be tuned. It can conveniently be done with this chunk of code

# In this version we are not tuning the number of trees, but we could.
# We tune mtry and min_n the number of obs in each terminal leaves (you don't want one leaf == 1 obs that's overfitting)
# mtry is the number of features that are randomly selected at each split. It is a good idea to tune it because it can have a big impact on the performance of the model
# Doing this is an argument if I have a lot of predictors/features. At each round, it is only a subsample of predictors that is used. 
rf_para <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_spec) %>% # extract the tuning parameters
  finalize(train_df) # here we have only 2 because we set trees to 100 not tune()
# finalize(train): we need to know the maximum number of features we could fit because it has not looked at the data yet
# it tells tidymodel that he can look at the data quickly to see how many features there are in the data

set.seed(20) # for reproducibility

# Set the tuning grid
# The tuning grid is the set of values of the tuning parameters we seek to evaluate. The larger the better
rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(rf_para,  # we use a latin hypercube here. 
                                size = 150, # 25 random combinations of mtry and min_n LOW! Increase in real life. There are good chances that the "true" combination is not in there
                                variogram_range = 0.75, # explore the space of the hyperparameters
                                original = TRUE)
set.seed(30)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_df, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = target) # stratified CV

rf_metrics <- metric_set(accuracy) # classification task

doParallel::registerDoParallel() # used parallel cores to run the computation

# tune the model, with the cross validation method defined, the grid and the metrics you set
rf_tune <- initial_flow_rfe %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds, grid = rf_grid, metrics = rf_metrics)


# select the best parameters for the model the tuning found
rf_best <- select_best(rf_tune)
rf_best# Trees again with X features at each time and X obs at terminal leaves
# 34 features, and 19 obs in terminal leaves

# Update the model with the best parameters found
rf_updated <- finalize_model(rf_spec,
                             rf_best) 

# add this to the initial workflow
workflow_new <- initial_flow_rfe %>%
  update_model(rf_updated)

# Fit the model on the training set
rf_fit_final <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = train_df_filtered) # fit on the training set

# Fit the model on the test set to evaluate performance
# Performance on the test set
rf_fit_final %>%
  predict(test_df_filtered) %>%
  bind_cols(test_df_filtered) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred_class)
# the accuracy is great but the kappa not that much (average)
# see if tuning the trees improve this in the future
